the development of BMI capabilities and the management approaches of established SMEs are key factors to foster BMI.
long term management orientation is a key driver of business model innovation in SMEs, and that open innovation, as a set of practices, is a precondition for business model innovation.

the management approach towards BMI is key for BMI in established SME, and the BMI capabilities that support the management approach are sensing customer needs, sensing technology options, conceptualizing, collaborating, and BMI strategy.

the development of BMI capabilities in SMEs.
the question of how SMEs can develop BMI and how this can be supported by their management approach and BMI capabilities.
the management approaches and capabilities that SMEs should develop in order to implement BMI, and the conditions under which BMI is more likely to occur.

the management approach of the company, together with the BMI capabilities, are key factors in the development of BMI.
the development of BMI is a complex phenomenon that is not linear but rather depends on a number of contingency factors that are interrelated and interact with each other.

the management approach towards business model innovation is a key antecedent of business model innovation in established SMEs, which can be achieved by developing a set of dynamic capabilities that foster business model innovation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the development of BMI is not a linear process but a complex one that depends on contingency conditions.

BMI in SMEs is a complex phenomenon that requires a configurational approach.
